input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 is the only governing law provision in the Agreement (no arbitration, jurisdiction, venue or dispute-forum language appears anywhere, including the miscellaneous Article 10 that runs to the signature block). The choice of law is New York, which is our preferred law, so element one of the preferred checklist is already met on the face of p0065. However, the Agreement designates no dispute forum at all, and a forum is a material element at both the preferred and the fallback level; without it neither party has consented to a court and either side could be pulled into HDI's New Jersey home courts or elsewhere. That failure of the forum element is material rather than a minor wording gap, so the clause does not sit at the fallback and we redline at the preferred level. The shortest complete fix keeps the existing law sentence untouched and adds one sentence giving the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction. This is not walk-away territory (no foreign venue or offshore arbitration seat), so a mutual New York County consent should be uncontroversial for HDI.

proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County forum to the New York governing law clause (Section 10.5).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10.5 already gives us New York law but names no forum, so we add exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our preferred governing law and venue position.

ops.text: Each Party irrevocably consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York over any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
